ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage stabilizing circuit composed of CW7805. On the left side is the input terminal Ui, and there is a capacitor C1 connected to the lower common ground line; on the right side is the output terminal U0, and there is a capacitor C2 connected to the ground line. The output terminal of CW7805 is connected to the upper right output node U0+. Resistor R1 is marked as 1 kΩ, connected between the output node U0+ and the middle node; resistor R2 is marked as 1 kΩ, connected between this middle node and ground. The common terminal of CW7805 is also connected to this middle node, and the common terminal current IW = 5 mA is marked in the figure as flowing toward this node. Reasoning: CW7805 maintains the voltage of the output terminal relative to the common terminal at 5 V, therefore the voltage across R1 is 5 V. R1 = 1 kΩ, so the current flowing through R1 is IR1 = 5 V / 1 kΩ = 5 mA. At the middle node, the 5 mA current of R1 and the common terminal current IW = 5 mA are added and then flow through R2, so IR2 = 10 mA. R2 = 1 kΩ, therefore the voltage on R2 is 10 mA × 1 kΩ = 10 V. The voltage from the output terminal to ground is equal to the 5 V on R1 plus the 10 V on R2, so U0 = 15 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image connections: upper resistor R1 connects from U0+ to the CW7805 common-pin junction, and lower resistor R2 connects from that junction to ground. Since CW7805 regulates output-to-common voltage to 5 V, the voltage across R1 is 5 V, so IR1=5 V/1 kΩ=5 mA. At the junction, add the given common-pin current IW=5 mA to the current through R1, so IR2=10 mA. The drop across R2 is then 10 mA×1 kΩ=10 V. Sum the two drops from output to ground: U0=5 V+10 V=15 V.

method.method_draft: Let Vx be the voltage of the junction of R1, R2, and the CW7805 common pin relative to ground. From the 7805 regulation condition read from the circuit, U0−Vx=5 V.
